items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee discusses Lester Young's performance of 'Black and Blue' in the forties. John Coltrane is mentioned by the interviewer only as a temporal marker ('before Coltrane, in the forties') to contextualize the era, not as someone the interviewee interacted with.

ctx.x: Beyond his fondest dream. Some guy walks in with him to Jimmy Ryan's one night and says, "You know what?" Says, "Milton Mezzrow's the only guy I know could make a clarinet sound like it's got hay fever. (Laughter).

I once heard, before the days of long solos, you know... before Coltrane, in the forties, , I think he was playing "Black and Blue." And he played...I'd never heard anybody play that long before, you know...fifteen minutes.
"Black and Blue" became red and pink...(laughter). But he was a good old...good old boy from Chicago. He was a good old boy.
